hints.tr: `sales["date"].min()` tek bir `Timestamp` veriyor; onda `.strftime(...)` ve `.day_name()` doğrudan çalışıyor.
hints.en: `sales["date"].min()` gives a single `Timestamp`; `.strftime(...)` and `.day_name()` work on it directly.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
import pandas as pd

sales = pd.read_csv("store_sales.csv")
sales["date"] = pd.to_datetime(sales["date"])

print(pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(sales["date"]))

first = sales["date"].min()
last = sales["date"].max()
print(first.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), last.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
print((last - first).days)
print(first.day_name())
```

The solution:

```python
import pandas as pd

sales = pd.read_csv("store_sales.csv")
sales["date"] = pd.to_datetime(sales["date"])

print(pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(sales["date"]))

first = sales["date"].min()
last = sales["date"].max()
print(first.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), last.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
print((last - first).days)
print(first.day_name())
```
